Compliance Audit Finding:
- Rule ID: RFC8221-ENCR_3DES
- Parameter: ESP Encryption
- Assigned Severity: HIGH
- Vulnerability Tag: SWEET32 (CVE-2016-2183)
- Description: 64-bit block cipher susceptible to birthday collision attacks after 32GB of data.

Perform an authoritative cryptographic compliance analysis explaining why this finding is classified as HIGH.

### Cryptanalytic Threat & Mathematical Analysis
The parameter `ESP Encryption` exhibits a fundamental cryptographic vulnerability: 3DES operates with a 64-bit block size. By the Birthday Paradox, identical ciphertext blocks (collisions) occur with high probability after approximately 2^32 blocks (32 GB of data transfer). In CBC mode, an adversary observing this collision can mathematically recover the XOR sum of the corresponding plaintexts, enabling full plaintext recovery.

### Primary Standards Grounding
Under governing standard [RFC 8221 §5] and [NIST SP 800-131A Rev. 2 §2], this algorithm is explicitly classified as unacceptable for production IPsec tunnels. The standards mandate deprecation due to demonstrated attack feasibility in enterprise and national security environments.

### System Impact & Blast Radius
Compromises ESP packet confidentiality on active high-throughput links. Traffic streams transferring >32GB of sensitive data can have credentials, session tokens, or sensitive payloads extracted via MitM traffic capture.

### Verified Actionable Remediation
To achieve full compliance, apply the following strongSwan `swanctl.conf` configuration upgrade:
```text
connections {
  vpn {
    esp_proposals = aes256gcm16-aes128gcm16
  }
}
```

Compliance Audit Finding:
- Rule ID: RFC8247-DH_GROUP_2
- Parameter: Diffie-Hellman Group
- Assigned Severity: CRITICAL
- Vulnerability Tag: Logjam (CVE-2015-4000)
- Description: 1024-bit MODP group vulnerable to Number Field Sieve precomputation.

Perform an authoritative cryptographic compliance analysis explaining why this finding is classified as CRITICAL.

### Cryptanalytic Threat & Mathematical Analysis
The parameter `Diffie-Hellman Group` exhibits a fundamental cryptographic vulnerability: MODP-1024 uses a standardized prime. The General Number Field Sieve (GNFS) algorithm allows an attacker with state-level compute resources to perform a one-time precomputation for the prime field, reducing individual Diffie-Hellman secret recoveries to simple online descent calculations solvable in real time.

### Primary Standards Grounding
Under governing standard [RFC 8247 §2.4] and [NIST SP 800-131A Rev. 2 §5], this algorithm is explicitly classified as unacceptable for production IPsec tunnels. The standards mandate deprecation due to demonstrated attack feasibility in enterprise and national security environments.

### System Impact & Blast Radius
Permits passive decryption of IKEv2 SA negotiations, resulting in total compromise of SKEYSEED and subsequent Child SA key derivations.

### Verified Actionable Remediation
To achieve full compliance, apply the following strongSwan `swanctl.conf` configuration upgrade:
```text
connections {
  vpn {
    proposals = aes256-sha256-ecp256,aes256-sha256-modp2048
  }
}
```

Compliance Audit Finding:
- Rule ID: RFC8221-AUTH_NONE_CBC
- Parameter: ESP Authentication
- Assigned Severity: CRITICAL
- Vulnerability Tag: Unauthenticated Encryption (Plaintext Oracle)
- Description: CBC mode without authentication allows bit-flipping and padding oracle attacks.

Perform an authoritative cryptographic compliance analysis explaining why this finding is classified as CRITICAL.

### Cryptanalytic Threat & Mathematical Analysis
The parameter `ESP Authentication` exhibits a fundamental cryptographic vulnerability: In CBC mode, modifying ciphertext block C_{i-1} predictably flips bits in decrypted plaintext block P_i. Without an Integrity Check Value (ICV), an active adversary can manipulate headers, inject forged commands, or mount Vaudenay padding oracle attacks.

### Primary Standards Grounding
Under governing standard [RFC 8221 §4] and [RFC 4303 §3.3.3], this algorithm is explicitly classified as unacceptable for production IPsec tunnels. The standards mandate deprecation due to demonstrated attack feasibility in enterprise and national security environments.

### System Impact & Blast Radius
Enables active Man-in-the-Middle attackers to decrypt ciphertext blocks by monitoring gateway error responses.

### Verified Actionable Remediation
To achieve full compliance, apply the following strongSwan `swanctl.conf` configuration upgrade:
```text
connections {
  vpn {
    esp_proposals = aes256gcm16,aes256-sha256
  }
}
```

Compliance Audit Finding:
- Rule ID: RFC9347-IP_TFS_OBFUSCATION
- Parameter: Traffic Flow Security
- Assigned Severity: INFO
- Vulnerability Tag: Side-Channel Defense (IP-TFS)
- Description: Fixed-size packets and constant bit-rate tunnel framing mitigate packet size/timing leakage.

Perform an authoritative cryptographic compliance analysis explaining why this finding is classified as INFO.

### Cryptanalytic Threat & Mathematical Analysis
The parameter `Traffic Flow Security` exhibits a fundamental cryptographic vulnerability: Standard ESP leaks application signatures through packet length distributions and Inter-Arrival Times (IAT). RFC 9347 IP-TFS employs AGGFRAG (Aggregation and Fragmentation) with fixed-size tunnel packets and synthetic padding, completely flattening traffic entropy to zero variance.

### Primary Standards Grounding
Under governing standard [RFC 9347 §2] and [RFC 9347 §8], this algorithm is explicitly classified as unacceptable for production IPsec tunnels. The standards mandate deprecation due to demonstrated attack feasibility in enterprise and national security environments.

### System Impact & Blast Radius
Neutralizes AI traffic classifiers and side-channel eavesdropping attacks attempting to identify VoIP or database queries.

### Verified Actionable Remediation
To achieve full compliance, apply the following strongSwan `swanctl.conf` configuration upgrade:
```text
# Deploy RFC 9347 IP-TFS framing:
swanctl --load-conns
# Enable fixed-rate traffic shaping with padding
```

Compliance Audit Finding:
- Rule ID: RFC7383-IKE_FRAGMENTATION
- Parameter: IKEv2 Protocol
- Assigned Severity: MEDIUM
- Vulnerability Tag: UDP Fragmentation Drop Risk
- Description: Large certificate chains without IKEv2 fragmentation cause packet drops on intermediate routers.

Perform an authoritative cryptographic compliance analysis explaining why this finding is classified as MEDIUM.

### Cryptanalytic Threat & Mathematical Analysis
The parameter `IKEv2 Protocol` exhibits a fundamental cryptographic vulnerability: X.509 certificate chains often exceed standard path MTU (1500 bytes), causing IP-level fragmentation. Firewalls and NAT gateways frequently drop IP fragments of UDP port 500/4500 packets, causing IKE_AUTH handshake timeouts.

### Primary Standards Grounding
Under governing standard [RFC 7383 §2.3] and [RFC 7296 §1.2], this algorithm is explicitly classified as unacceptable for production IPsec tunnels. The standards mandate deprecation due to demonstrated attack feasibility in enterprise and national security environments.

### System Impact & Blast Radius
Causes intermittent VPN connection failures during certificate authentication across carrier networks.

### Verified Actionable Remediation
To achieve full compliance, apply the following strongSwan `swanctl.conf` configuration upgrade:
```text
connections {
  vpn {
    fragmentation = yes
  }
}
```

Compliance Audit Finding:
- Rule ID: RFC8784-POST_QUANTUM_PPK
- Parameter: Post-Quantum Security
- Assigned Severity: INFO
- Vulnerability Tag: Harvest Now, Decrypt Later Defense
- Description: Post-Quantum Pre-Shared Keys (PPK) protect against future quantum Shor's algorithm factoring.

Perform an authoritative cryptographic compliance analysis explaining why this finding is classified as INFO.

### Cryptanalytic Threat & Mathematical Analysis
The parameter `Post-Quantum Security` exhibits a fundamental cryptographic vulnerability: Shor's algorithm on cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) will break standard Diffie-Hellman and RSA. RFC 8784 injects a 256-bit symmetric pre-shared key (PPK) into the SKEYSEED derivation: SKEYSEED = prf(Ni | Nr, SK_d | PPK).

### Primary Standards Grounding
Under governing standard [RFC 8784 §6] and [NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 Table 1], this algorithm is explicitly classified as unacceptable for production IPsec tunnels. The standards mandate deprecation due to demonstrated attack feasibility in enterprise and national security environments.

### System Impact & Blast Radius
Guarantees that encrypted sessions recorded today cannot be decrypted when quantum computers emerge.

### Verified Actionable Remediation
To achieve full compliance, apply the following strongSwan `swanctl.conf` configuration upgrade:
```text
connections {
  vpn {
    ppk_id = enterprise-quantum-ppk-01
    ppk_required = yes
  }
}
```

    proposals = aes256-sha256-ecp256
